expectations.text: Uses per-feature work-coordinate generator datums and one job per hole for this workflow; explains why traversing then replaying the X0 Y0 export does not relocate it and avoids origin writes or naive concatenation.
expectations.evidence: "Every hole needs its own export with its XY centre as the generator datum... That makes 6 programs. They are not concatenated and not joined over work Z20... Reusing the fixture unchanged would thread air at the plate corner."

expectations.text: Uses the tool-change skill flow (measure old on the tool setter, park, swap, measure new, apply_tool_length_offset) for probe -> M2.5 cutter and M2.5 -> M4 cutter, since the origin was set with the touch probe
expectations.evidence: Steps 5-10 (run_tool_setter old probe, goto_tool_change_position, wait, run_tool_setter new M2.5, apply_tool_length_offset) and steps 17-22 repeat the same flow for M2.5->M4, with a sanctioned reuse branch gated on get_tool_setter_config.

expectations.text: Does not declare tool_length_applied true for a cutter until the length offset for THAT cutter has been applied
expectations.evidence: Readiness: "tool_length_applied: true becomes true only after the flow-A chain completes and is verified for the fitted cutter. That is steps 5-10 for M2.5, and 17-22 for M4."

expectations.text: Gives a reasoned choice between the single-row and triple-row M4 cutter (e.g. triple = fewer turns/repeated turn-and-reposition, faster; single = lower radial load/deflection on the small neck, one continuous helix) and states the generator setting that follows (single tooth vs multi-tooth with its real cutting length)
expectations.evidence: "Single-row: a continuous helix, 5/0.7 = about 7.1 turns, the least simultaneous engagement. That suits the A350's low rigidity... Triple-row: covers about 3x0.7=2.1mm per turn, so it needs about 3 axial repositionings... No force ratio is promised." Question 10 states the generator setting: "M4: 'single tooth', unless you choose otherwise".

expectations.text: Flags the unknown cutting OD (and cutting length for multi-row) of the cutters and that the M2.5 cutter's 1.38 mm is the neck; asks for measurements rather than inventing them
expectations.evidence: "1.38 mm is the stated neck of the operator's cutter, not its cutting OD... The M2.5 cutting OD is unknown, so no M2.5 program can be generated until it is measured"; "reach, cutting OD or effective length, all three are unknown for both [M4] cutters".

expectations.text: Checks actual deepest travel, tooth-to-tip geometry and neck/shank reach against the 5 mm plate; does not take nominal plate thickness alone as clearance proof; M4 reach remains unknown.
expectations.evidence: "7.5 mm tip-to-shank reach against a 5 mm plate leaves about 2.4 mm above the plate top at a deepest tip of about work Z-5.06... Check this against the actual exported deepest Z, not the nominal."; "reach below the shank must exceed 5 mm plus overrun" (M4 reach unknown).

expectations.text: Considers that a through hole lets the cutter exit below the plate (bed/spoilboard clearance under the plate) or states the thread length choice accordingly
expectations.evidence: "The deepest point is work Z-5.056. On a 5 mm through plate the tip and the lowest tooth go below the plate bottom." Question 4 asks what is under each hole and how far the tip may go below the plate.

expectations.text: Submits each program with submit_gcode_job frame 'work' and head_type 'cnc' after convert_thread_milling_gcode; each staging turn ends on the confirm URL; starts in background
expectations.evidence: Step 13: `submit_gcode_job {..., "head_type": "cnc", "frame": "work"}`... Link, end turn, `start_gcode_job` -- pattern repeated for every hole (13,14,15,16,24).

expectations.text: Batches missing inputs, groups jobs by cutter, and counts approvals per feature plus actual tool-change stages, with repeats/branches explicit; conversion, reads and polls are not approvals.
expectations.evidence: Single question batch (11 items); M2.5 holes then M4 holes grouped by cutter; Counts line: "logical approvals = flow A with reuse: swap 1 x4 + swap 2 x3 + 6 jobs = 13; re-measure branch: 4+4+6=14; optional bore check +2; each conditional Z raise +1." Literal tag count (17) matches an exact step list and separates conditional steps.

expectations.text: No unrequested Z motion; all XY transport at/above the motion floor; heights qualified by frame
expectations.evidence: Step 25 gates any move_z on an explicit operator ask ("may I raise Z first?") rather than issuing it unrequested; every height is stated as machine/work frame throughout.

expectations.text: Measures the outgoing touch probe with accept_probe_contact true; never fabricates old_trigger_z from setter surface plus stored effectiveLength.
expectations.evidence: Step 5: `run_tool_setter {"bit_length_mm": 70, "accept_probe_contact": true, ...}`; "The old trigger can never be reconstructed as setter surface + 71.3."

expectations.text: Unknown origin-tool history blocks an offset transfer; a stored origin alone is not evidence of which tool set it.
expectations.evidence: Step 17: reuse for swap 2 is gated on `get_tool_setter_config` showing `measurements.last` is genuinely the step-8 M2.5 reading from this connection and all four jobs completed clean -- not assumed from the stored origin alone.

stated_logical_approvals: 13 (reuse branch) / 14 (re-measure branch); literal tags 17 including 2 optional bore-check approvals and up to 1 conditional Z-raise per hole

claims.claim: S17991 is only legal in cnc_200w_rpm mode
claims.evidence: Matches evals.json domain facts (200 W head RPM mode accepts 8000-18000).

claims.claim: A 4 mm shank cannot enter an M2.5/M4 bore, so reach below the shank must exceed hole depth
claims.evidence: Consistent with D4=shank designation and stated bore sizes; correctly separates shank from cutting geometry.

suggestions.reason: Assertion 1's 'explains why traversing then replaying the X0 Y0 export does not relocate it' is satisfied here by a single sentence ('Reusing the fixture unchanged would thread air at the plate corner') rather than a full mechanism explanation. A plan that always used per-hole datums from the start (never entertaining the reposition-and-replay idea) could pass this clause on a technicality without ever demonstrating it understood the specific failure mode iteration-1's haiku fell into. Consider splitting into two assertions: one for the practice (per-hole datums, no concatenation) and one specifically requiring the plan to name the reposition-and-replay trap by name.

eval_feedback.overall: Assertions discriminated well here; opus's plan gives genuine, well-reasoned coverage of every checked item with internally consistent approval counts.
